newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy doing "exceptionally well" - Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy doing "exceptionally well" - Greenspan.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said on Wednesday that the economy is doing "exceptionally well" and sought to reassure lawmakers that the central bank would not act to undermine that.
He told a House Banking subcommittee that faster economic growth or a drop in the unemployment rate on their own would not be enough to spark an interest rate increase by the Fed.
Asked if there was a single jobless rate that would trigger a rate rise by the Fed, Greenspan replied, "No."
Greenspan also took issue with those who argue that faster growth alone will lead to higher inflation.
"It (is not) growth per se that ... we respond to, it's evidences of inflationary imbalances," he said.
"It is certainly the case ... that the economy is doing exceptionally well from our point of view," he added.
Greenspan, however, acknowledged that he was concerned about growing income inequality in the United States, but said it was not clear what monetary policy can do about that.
